verdict: Flex grew sales 25% to $8.5B as its Cloud & Power Infrastructure business — soon to be spun off as Axiom — surged 54% on data-center demand; GAAP profit was $263M.

segments.name: Integrated Technology Solutions
segments.note: Manufacturing for consumer, lifestyle and connected-home products (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

segments.name: Regulated Manufacturing Solutions
segments.note: Manufacturing for health and other regulated industries, where quality rules are strictest (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

segments.name: Cloud & Power Infrastructure
segments.note: Data-center power, cooling and IT infrastructure — up 54% on AI data-center demand. Flex plans to spin this segment off as a separate company named Axiom (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs of running the global manufacturing network.

opex.name: Intangible amortization
opex.note: Amortization of intangible assets bought in acquisitions.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $69M, partly offset by $13M of interest income, $7M of other income and $5M of equity earnings from unconsolidated affiliates — a net $44M drag.
footerNote: Cost of revenue is cost of sales of $7,664M plus $15M of restructuring charges that Flex reports inside cost of sales.

takeaways.title: The spin-off segment is the growth story
takeaways.text: Cloud & Power Infrastructure sales rose 54% to $2.5B as AI data centers scramble for power and cooling. Flex is spinning it off as 'Axiom' and bought EPC Power to complete the power portfolio.

takeaways.title: Record adjusted EPS
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS hit a record $1.18 versus $0.70 GAAP. The gap includes roughly $91M of legal and other costs — mostly for the planned spin-off — plus restructuring and stock compensation.

takeaways.title: Thin margins, by design
takeaways.text: Contract manufacturing runs on thin margins: a 4.9% GAAP operating margin (7.1% adjusted) on $8.5B of sales. Profitability depends on mix shifting toward power and regulated work.

oneTimers: Costs of roughly $91M in the quarter — mainly legal and other costs of the planned Cloud & Power Infrastructure spin-off, plus $19M of acquisition costs — are excluded from Flex's adjusted results.
Restructuring charges were $15M inside cost of sales; a year ago the quarter also carried impairments from the missile strike on Flex's Mukachevo, Ukraine plant.
